model: iCM chiller plant manager, option 184 (Daikin Applied Europe)
applies_to: Daikin Applied Europe chiller plants run by the iCM software (option 184) on the master MicroTech 4 chiller: a master plus up to seven slave chillers, with optional pump (iPM), cooling tower (iCT) and pump group (iSM) management.
summary: iCM is a software option on a MicroTech 4 chiller that makes it the master of a multi-chiller plant: it stages a master and up to seven slaves and tracks system load, demand limit and the standby unit. Version 5.00 also manages evaporator/condenser pumps (iPM), up to ten cooling towers (iCT) and iSM pump groups. BACnet IP or BACnet MS/TP comes from a POL908/POL904 module or the onboard software option on that controller. Most objects are read-only plant data per chiller; writable ones cover master enable, staging priorities, standby unit, pump and tower network setpoints and alarm resets.
notes: The guide does not spell out "iCM"; Daikin's product pages call it the Intelligent Chiller Manager. It is the plant-manager software (option 184) running on the master chiller.
SCMType (MV 1101) shows the plant type: Master/Slave, iCM Standard or iCM Advanced. Slave, energy, heat recovery, free-cooling, pump, tower, defrost and iSM objects only apply when configured.
Each chiller's own unit objects (enable, setpoints, alarms) are on its own controller; this list is the plant-level view.
The guide prints multistate objects as MSV; they are listed here as MV. Rows printed "as <other object>" are given that object's state texts or units.
Revision 11/2023 matches iCM software 5.00 (adds iCT cooling towers, system heat recovery, free cooling, defrost, iSM and iCM Expanded).
Units "°Dc" in the guide are shown as dK; counters and ranges are shown without units.

integration.summary: Read the plant view from the master chiller: system run state, common leaving water temperature, active setpoint, load and the state of each chiller. Write only the few plant settings exposed (master enable, staging priorities, standby unit, pump/tower network setpoints) and use the alarm reset MVs. Start/stop and setpoints for individual chillers are not in this list.

minimum_points.name: EvapPM'ClearAlm
minimum_points.why: Reset evaporator pump manager alarms (2 = Reset)

minimum_points.name: MasterData'State
minimum_points.why: Master chiller state, incl. Alarm / ComErr

integration.enable: The guide exposes no plant start/stop or plant setpoint object. MasterEnablingSp (MV 1324) enables or disables the master unit, and the per-unit cooling/heating priorities (MV 1325-1340) and StandbyChillerSp (MV 51) set the staging; the guide does not describe how the plant itself is enabled from a BMS.
integration.remote_sensors: Pump speed and bypass control take network setpoints (AV 1370/1373/1376/1382/1385 evaporator, AV 1411/1414/1417/1422/1425 condenser) and the tower leaving water control takes iCT'LwtCtrl'SpNtwk (AV 1462); the guide does not say how these are selected over the local values.
setup: BACnet IP comes from the POL908 module or, on MicroTech 4, the onboard BACnet IP software option (enabled under Commissioning > Configuration > Software Options with an unlock password).
BACnet MS/TP comes from the POL904 module or the onboard BACnet MS/TP software option.
BACnet IP defaults: device instance 1, UDP port 47808, DHCP off; set Apply Changes = Yes after editing, which restarts the controller.

BACnet MS/TP module defaults: MAC address 24, 38400 baud, Max Master 127, Max Info Frames 1; the device instance is derived from the production number and date code. Cycle power after changing the address.
EDE files are regenerated each time the BACnet server starts and can be downloaded by FTP from the POL908; re-export them after any configuration change.
gotchas: Several multistate objects use 0 = NULL as the first state; write the real value (e.g. 2 = Enable), not 0.
Staging priorities (MV 1325-1340, 1-8) and StandbyChillerSp are settings; write them once, not cyclically.
Slave state objects are named S1State-S7State, not SlaveDataN'State like the other slave objects.
There is no single plant alarm object: watch the master/slave State MVs, the slave CommErr/Missing BVs, the pump/tower GenAlm MVs and ConfigErrReason.
The guide prints the same description for several bypass and speed network setpoints; check the object name to tell them apart.
